crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Credit Scoring with Alternative Data
children.blurb: Credit scoring with alternative data means using information beyond the traditional credit bureau file to estimate the likelihood that a borrower repays.

children.name: Covenant Extraction
children.blurb: Covenant extraction is the work of pulling the specific terms and conditions out of loan and bond documentation and turning them into structured data.

children.name: Predicting Distress and Default
children.blurb: Predicting distress and default covers the models and data used to estimate whether a borrower, issuer or counterparty will fail to meet its obligations.

children.name: Modelling the Yield Curve
children.blurb: Modelling the yield curve means estimating the relationship between interest rates and time to maturity for a given issuer or market, then using that relationship to price bonds, measure rate risk and value derivatives.

children.name: Stress Testing Structured Credit
children.blurb: Stress testing structured credit means asking how a pool of securitised assets, and the tranches issued against it, behave when conditions turn worse than the base case.

sections.body: Fixed income and credit risk is the part of finance that asks whether a borrower will pay back and what happens if they do not. Artificial intelligence is now used across that question, from scoring loan applicants to reading the legal documents that govern a bond. In credit scoring, models built on alternative data such as transaction records or utility payments estimate default probability for people with thin credit files. In covenant extraction, language models pull the financial tests and triggers out of indenture and loan agreements so analysts do not have to read hundreds of pages by hand. Distress prediction models scan filings, news and market prices for early signs that a company is heading toward default. On the trading side, models fit the yield curve and run stress tests on structured credit portfolios under different rate and default scenarios.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Credit scoring with alternative data is deployed at scale by lenders, but the models are hard to audit and regulators in several jurisdictions require explanations that many machine learning systems cannot easily give. Covenant extraction works well on standard clauses and struggles with unusual wording, cross references and amendments, so human review remains standard. Distress prediction has real signal but modest accuracy over long horizons, and it tends to flag companies that are already in trouble rather than foreseeing trouble months ahead. Yield curve modelling is a mature statistical problem where machine learning offers incremental gains at best. Stress testing structured credit is the least settled area, because the data is sparse, the instruments are complex and the tail scenarios that matter most are the ones with the fewest historical examples.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages here follow the chain from individual borrower to portfolio. Credit Scoring with Alternative Data covers the entry point, how models judge borrowers who lack traditional credit histories and what that means for access and fairness. Covenant Extraction deals with the documents that sit behind corporate loans and bonds, and the practical task of turning legal language into structured data. Predicting Distress and Default moves from a single borrower to the question of which firms are likely to fail, using filings and market signals. Modelling the Yield Curve supplies the interest rate backdrop that prices every fixed income instrument. Stress Testing Structured Credit brings these threads together, taking the rates from the yield curve and the default estimates from distress models and applying them to pools of securitised debt under adverse conditions.
